content: Information for Patients Patients should be informed about specific substances they must avoid while taking Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. They should also be instructed to promptly report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness. Additionally, patients must notify any healthcare provider prescribing new medications that they are currently taking Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. Skeletal Muscle Post-marketing reports have documented cases of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis in patients taking ezetimibe, regardless of causality. Most of these cases occurred in individuals who were already on a statin before starting ezetimibe. However, rhabdomyolysis has also been reported, albeit very rarely, in patients on ezetimibe monotherapy or when ezetimibe was combined with other agents known to increase the risk of rhabdomyolysis, such as fibrates. Therefore, Ezetimibe/Simvastatin is not recommended for use in these patients. Drug Interactions Ezetimibe/Simvastatin CYP3A4 Interactions: Potent inhibitors of CYP3A4, such as itraconazole, ketoconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, and large quantities of grapefruit juice (more than 1 quart daily), can increase the risk of myopathy by reducing the elimination of simvastatin. Lipid-lowering drugs: The risk of myopathy is heightened when Ezetimibe/Simvastatin is used with gemfibrozil, other fibrates, or high doses of niacin (≥1 g/day). Other Drug Interactions Amiodarone or Verapamil: Co-administration with higher doses of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin increases the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Cholestyramine: This reduces the absorption of ezetimibe by approximately 55%, potentially diminishing its LDL-C-lowering effect. Cyclosporine or Danazol: These increase the risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, especially at higher doses of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. Digoxin: Simvastatin slightly elevates plasma digoxin levels, necessitating monitoring when initiating Ezetimibe/Simvastatin. Fibrates: Co-administration with fibrates is not recommended due to the potential for gallstone formation and lack of established safety and efficacy. Warfarin: Simvastatin can modestly enhance the effects of warfarin, increasing prothrombin time (INR). Monitoring is required when starting or adjusting Ezetimibe/Simvastatin in patients on warfarin. Ezetimibe Fenofibrate: Co-administration increases ezetimibe concentrations by approximately 1.5-fold. Gemfibrozil: Co-administration increases ezetimibe concentrations by approximately 1.7-fold. Simvastatin Propranolol: Co-administration reduces the peak concentration (Cmax) of simvastatin, but the clinical significance of this finding is unclear. CNS Toxicity In animal studies, simvastatin caused optic nerve degeneration in dogs at doses producing plasma drug levels significantly higher than those seen in humans. Similar findings were observed with other drugs in this class. Additionally, high doses of simvastatin caused CNS vascular lesions, including perivascular hemorrhage, edema, and necrosis of small vessels, in dogs. Cataracts were observed in rats and dogs at doses producing plasma drug levels much higher than those in humans. Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, Impairment of Fertility Ezetimibe/Simvastatin No animal studies have been conducted to evaluate the carcinogenicity or fertility effects of the combination. However, in vitro studies showed no evidence of mutagenicity or clastogenicity. Simvastatin Carcinogenicity studies in mice and rats showed an increased incidence of liver tumors, thyroid neoplasms, and other adenomas at high doses. Pregnancy Ezetimibe/Simvastatin Vytorin is contraindicated in pregnancy (Category X). It should be discontinued immediately if pregnancy is detected. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception and be informed of the potential risks. Ezetimibe Animal studies showed no embryolethal effects, but skeletal abnormalities were observed at high doses. Ezetimibe crosses the placenta, and co-administration with statins during pregnancy increases the risk of reproductive toxicity. Simvastatin Simvastatin was not teratogenic in animal studies, but skeletal malformations were observed with other drugs in this class. Most cases involved drug discontinuation during the first trimester. Labor and Delivery The effects of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin on labor and delivery are unknown. Nursing Mothers Ezetimibe is excreted into the milk of nursing rats, and it is unknown whether ezetimibe or simvastatin is excreted into human breast milk. Due to the potential for serious adverse effects in nursing infants, women should not take Vytorin while breastfeeding. Pediatric Use Ezetimibe/Simvastatin There is insufficient data to establish the safety and efficacy of Vytorin in pediatric patients. Ezetimibe Limited data are available for adolescents aged 10-18 years, but treatment in children under 10 years is not recommended. Simvastatin Simvastatin has been studied in adolescents with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. The safety profile was similar to placebo, and no effects on growth or sexual maturation were observed. Doses above 40 mg have not been studied in this population. Simvastatin has not been studied in children under 10 years or pre-menarchal girls. Geriatric Use Clinical studies included 792 patients aged 65 and older, with 176 aged 75 and older. The safety profile of Ezetimibe/Simvastatin was similar between older and younger patients, but increased sensitivity in some elderly individuals cannot be ruled out.
